title: County of Béarn
capsule: Béarn was a Pyrenean domain that functioned as a de facto sovereign principality, its rulers famously asserting they held it from God and no earthly lord. Gaston III Fébus (r. 1343–1391) made that claim explicit in 1347 and ran a brilliant court at Orthez while playing the Hundred Years' War powers against each other. The attestation window of 1385–1453 covers the reigns of Gaston IV and his successors under the houses of Grailly and Foix-Navarre; the territory eventually passed through Jeanne d'Albret to her son Henry, who became Henry IV of France in 1589 and united Béarn with the French crown by royal decree in 1620.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Béarn's territory is geographically well defined by Pyrenean topography and documented in French and Navarrese royal records; the attestation window captures only part of its longer autonomous history.
